sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house fast in East Brunswick, NJ?
sections.html:
East Brunswick sellers can list on the open market, sell directly to a cash buyer, or sell to a neighbor or relative without an agent. Speed is the deciding factor. A listing in a township this size can attract strong interest, but it still means staging, showings, a buyer's inspection and a lender's appraisal. A direct sale trades some of that price for a closing date you control.

The Census Bureau estimated East Brunswick's population at 50,678 on July 1, 2025, up from 49,715 in 2020. Eight in ten occupied homes are lived in by their owners. Common reasons to sell fast include an inherited house, a tired rental, or a house that needs more updating than its owner wants to take on.

  • Traditional listing: best fit for a house in good order with a flexible timeline.
  • Direct cash sale: best fit when the house needs work, has tenants, or must close on a fixed date.
  • For-sale-by-owner: workable if you know the paperwork, but the township smoke and carbon monoxide certificate still applies.

sections.h2: How did East Brunswick become a commuter township?
sections.html:
East Brunswick was incorporated on February 28, 1860, carved from parts of Monroe and North Brunswick. It stayed mostly farmland until suburban building began in the 1930s, and the New Jersey Turnpike extension of 1952 set off the big surge: the population went from 5,699 in 1950 to 19,965 in 1960. The Old Bridge section in the southeast has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1977.

Geography still shapes lots and prices. The township covers 21.78 square miles of land on the south bank of the Raritan River. Lawrence Brook and Farrington Lake run along the western edge, the South River marks the east, and Manalapan Brook drains much of the south. It touches Edison, Helmetta, Milltown, Monroe, New Brunswick, North Brunswick, Old Bridge, Sayreville, South River, South Brunswick and Spotswood. Since the 2000 census, the Census Bureau has placed New Jersey's center of population inside East Brunswick.

sections.h2: How do Route 18, the Turnpike and buses affect an East Brunswick sale?
sections.html:
Commuting is a large part of the pitch. East Brunswick sits at Exit 9 of the Turnpike, and Route 18 crosses the east side, giving access to New Brunswick, U.S. Route 1 and the Shore. County routes 527 and 535 also pass through, and the Garden State Parkway and Interstate 287 are a short drive away in neighboring towns. Midtown Manhattan and Center City Philadelphia are each a 45 to 60 minute drive depending on traffic, and Newark Liberty International Airport is about 24 miles away.

NJ Transit runs the 138 to the Port Authority Bus Terminal and the 68 to Jersey City, and local routes 811, 815 and 818 serve the township. Suburban Transit buses to New York leave from the Transportation Center and Tower Center every 10 to 15 minutes, with trips taking 30 to 50 minutes. The township has about 206 miles of road, of which roughly 176 are municipal.

The Census Bureau lists the average trip to work at 36.5 minutes for East Brunswick residents, against 30.5 minutes statewide, which fits a township that sends so many people toward New York.

sections.h2: What business and shopping draws support East Brunswick values?
sections.html: Brunswick Square Mall opened in 1970 at Route 18 and Rues Lane and has about 769,000 square feet of leasable space. Near the Turnpike and Route 18 stand the two 23-story Tower Center office towers and a 12-story Hilton, and Wipro opened its U.S. headquarters there in March 2023. At the quieter end, Giamarese Farm and Orchards has run on 35 acres of Fresh Ponds Road since 1941.

sections.h2: Which schools serve East Brunswick homes?
sections.html:
East Brunswick Public Schools runs 11 schools for pre-kindergarten through grade 12 and enrolled 8,163 students in 2024-25. Eight elementary schools cover the early grades: Bowne-Munro, Central, Chittick, Frost, Irwin, Lawrence Brook, Memorial and Warnsdorfer. Hammarskjold Upper Elementary takes grades 5 and 6, Churchill Junior High takes grades 7 to 9, and East Brunswick High School takes grades 10 to 12. Eighth graders anywhere in Middlesex County can also apply to the tuition-free Middlesex County Magnet Schools, which include a campus in East Brunswick.

Buyers will ask which elementary school a street feeds, so confirm that with the district before you list.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for East Brunswick housing?
sections.html:
Census estimates for 2020 through 2024 put the median owner-occupied home at $521,900, about $67,500 above the statewide median of $454,400, and 80.0 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. About 58 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree or more, and a third of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: Do I need a Certificate of Occupancy to sell in East Brunswick?
sections.html:
No. The township's construction page states that East Brunswick does not require or issue a Certificate of Occupancy for residential resale or rentals. A residential property gets its certificate when it is built, and after that only the new improvements are inspected when work is done. Call Construction Inspection at 732-390-6875 with questions.

Fire safety is a separate track. Carbon monoxide alarms have been required in one and two family homes since April 7, 2003, placed near the bedrooms. The township code also gained a new provision in 2025 through Ordinance 25-30, which requires smoke and carbon monoxide detector inspections and certificates for the sale, lease or occupancy of residential units. As introduced, the fee was $50 per unit when requested more than 10 business days before the change of occupant, $75 for 4 to 10 business days, and $125 for less than 4, with a $20 charge for re-inspection. Ask the township for the current schedule and book early, because the last-minute fee is the highest.

sections.h2: What does a sale cost a seller in East Brunswick?
sections.html:
The seller owes New Jersey's realty transfer fee when the deed is recorded. Applying the state's schedule to a sale at the Census median of $521,900 gives roughly $4,385, and sales above $1,000,000 add a graduated percentage fee on top.

  • Transfer fee: paid by the seller at recording, using the state's tiered rate per $500 of price.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate: a township charge that rises as closing approaches.
  • Mortgage payoff and liens: deducted from proceeds at closing.
  • Tax form: the seller signs GIT/REP paperwork with the deed, which also settles whether a nonresident seller must prepay.

sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded for an East Brunswick house?
sections.html: The Middlesex County Clerk records deeds at the County Administration Building, 75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick. The posted hours run Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:10 p.m., and you must arrive by 4 p.m. The registry number is 732-745-3002. The county's posted fee schedule lists $45 for the first deed page and $10 for each additional page, with a $6 name fee when it applies. The county also runs a free Property Alert service that sends email notices when a document matching your property is recorded.

sections.h2: What if my East Brunswick house has been a short-term rental?
sections.html: The township code has a Short-Term Rental chapter, Chapter 182, which the council amended through Ordinance 25-34 in 2025. If you have hosted guests, read the current chapter or call the township before you disclose the house's rental history to a buyer.

faqs.q: Does East Brunswick require a resale inspection?
faqs.a: The township does not require a Certificate of Occupancy for residential resale. It does require smoke and carbon monoxide detector certification on sale under a 2025 ordinance, so ask the township how to schedule it.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in East Brunswick?
faqs.a: The timeline is set by the contract. Without a lender's appraisal, closing depends mostly on the title search, the smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, and the deed filing with the Middlesex County Clerk.

faqs.q: Who pays the realty transfer fee in East Brunswick?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at recording. At the Census median value of $521,900 it works out to about $4,385 under the state's rate schedule.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed after an East Brunswick closing?
faqs.a: At the Middlesex County Clerk's Office, 75 Bayard Street, 4th floor, New Brunswick. The registry number is 732-745-3002.

faqs.q: Can I sell an East Brunswick house that still has tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The ordinance covers sale, lease and other occupancy, so plan the smoke and carbon monoxide inspection around the tenants' move-out or the closing date.
